independence: The triage agent wrote none of the guides and ran no walkthrough. It changed no guide text and no evidence record.
commands: git rev-list --no-merges <merge>^1..<merge> (for each first-parent merge, to map commits to pull requests)
git diff 067c1646829df85e62b809ee9157921e867c84e7..HEAD -- scripts/seed CONTEXT.md compose.dev.yml .env.example docs/DEPLOYMENT.md messages/en-US.json
git diff 067c1646829df85e62b809ee9157921e867c84e7..HEAD -- <per-file inspections named in candidates[].inspectedFiles>

git log --format=%h <range> -- docs/user-guides/<guide>.md and git show <commit>:docs/user-guides/<guide>.md | sha256sum (to find the commit whose text matches each edited guide's evidence contentSha256)
git diff --word-diff=plain <matching commit> HEAD -- docs/user-guides/<guide>.md (for the eight edited guides)
method: I listed the application diff from 067c1646, from 3fa407e3 and from 648f99ec, and mapped each of the 88 app commits since 067c1646 to its first-parent pull request or marked it a direct commit on dev. I grouped the commits by product area and read their messages, the messages/en-US.json diff, the CONTEXT.md and seed diffs, and the code diffs behind each area. For each of the 50 candidates I read the guide at HEAD and its evidence sources, intersected the sources with the diff, grepped the guide for the changed labels and concepts, and opened the code for every claim a change could reach. For the six guides with evidence at 3fa407e3, the 3fa407e3 to 067c1646 range was already reviewed compatible in DOC-030 compat (compat/compat.json); I checked 067c1646 to HEAD for them. For the eight edited guides I found the commit whose text matches the evidence hash and diffed from there.

priorRange.note: All six were compatible at 067c1646. Their decisions here cover 067c1646 to 4ca41822.

limitations: Source review only. I ran no walkthrough, lab, build or test.
I judged guide text at HEAD 4ca41822. The worktree held uncommitted edits by other seats to seven of the eight edited guides and edition.json while I worked; I did not read or judge those edits.

Every compat replay runs on a lab built from 4ca41822. #1156 (00528360) changed the seed's random draws after the Business Owner pick, and 17179939 renamed the bootstrap Administrator to Devon Calloway (devon@helix.example). A replay step that relies on a seeded record's exact team, owner or name may fail; that is a script update, not a guide change. claude-live/phase-passwords.mjs still lists blair@helix.example.
DocuSign draft preparation stays off by default (SIGNING_PREPARATION_ENABLED). Claims about preparation, Resume and recovery states can only be checked on a stand-in or live lab.
configure-analysis's replay needs a live provider key, as in DOC-030.
findings: Possible guide or product conflict: first-run (text added in 1f2e77e1) says removing the last allowed domain disables the Business switches without changing their values, but PUT /auth/allowed-domains (3e91951f) stores password, magic link and SSO as off for Business Users. authentication-and-email and portal-sign-in do not yet say that an empty list stops every Business User signing in.
The app no longer offers whole-Document deletion anywhere (hardDeleteDocument has no caller after dd28e33d). archive-and-delete-documents is built around that action.
electronic-signing (blocked) still says Open Signatures, then select Prepare Envelope; b6a0bcfd renamed the trigger to Send for signature in both modes.
